lines: Robert B. Jackson was the son of  Wesley Jackson  and his wife, Elizabeth.
in Northwest Fork Hundred, Sussex Co., DE. He died on 29 December,
, still living in Sussex Co., DE . He is buried at the Indian Mission Church with his wife,  Lydia Ann Wright . Lydia was born on 2 February,
. Her photo can be found in the Nanticoke Indian Photo Book.
Robert appears with his parents in the

, however, Robert was married and living in his own household with his wife and 2 children (Mary Elizabeth, age 2 and John A., age 1). Living in the same household was James Wright, age 7. James was probably related to Lydia's family. Dave Wright, Lydia's uncle, and his family were living next door.
, however, he was living in Milford Hundred, Sussex Co., DE. and his occupation had changed to "farmer".

Robert's death certificate lists his age at the time of his death as 73 years, 10 months & 15 days. He was called a farmer, a widower and colored. The cause of death was listed as pneumonia and he was shown living in Millsboro, Indian River Hundred, Sussex Co., DE.

The death certificate lists the place of burial as Johnson's Chapel which was the name of the original Indian Mission Church and, in fact, his gravemarker (and Lydia's) is to be found there. It is now much weathered and cannot be read but I copied the inscription many years ago. The death certificate lists his mother's name as "Heslin" but the census clearly lists Elizabeth or "Lizzie".

Robert B Jackson
Preserved Primary Document • jacksnr2.htm
Robert B. Jackson was the son of  Wesley Jackson  and his wife, Elizabeth.
He was born on 15 February,
1842
in Northwest Fork Hundred, Sussex Co., DE. He died on 29 December,
1915
, still living in Sussex Co., DE . He is buried at the Indian Mission Church with his wife,  Lydia Ann Wright . Lydia was born on 2 February,
1848
and died 3 May,
1901
. Her photo can be found in the Nanticoke Indian Photo Book.
Robert appears with his parents in the
1850
and
1860
DE. census records.
By
1870
, however, Robert was married and living in his own household with his wife and 2 children (Mary Elizabeth, age 2 and John A., age 1). Living in the same household was James Wright, age 7. James was probably related to Lydia's family. Dave Wright, Lydia's uncle, and his family were living next door.
Robert's occupation in
1870
was listed as "seaman". By
1880
, however, he was living in Milford Hundred, Sussex Co., DE. and his occupation had changed to "farmer".
Robert's death certificate lists his age at the time of his death as 73 years, 10 months & 15 days. He was called a farmer, a widower and colored. The cause of death was listed as pneumonia and he was shown living in Millsboro, Indian River Hundred, Sussex Co., DE.
The death certificate lists the place of burial as Johnson's Chapel which was the name of the original Indian Mission Church and, in fact, his gravemarker (and Lydia's) is to be found there. It is now much weathered and cannot be read but I copied the inscription many years ago. The death certificate lists his mother's name as "Heslin" but the census clearly lists Elizabeth or "Lizzie".

Robert B. Jackson was the son of Wesley Jackson and his wife, Elizabeth. He was born on 15 February, 1842 in Northwest Fork Hundred, Sussex Co., DE. He died on 29 December, 1915, still living in Sussex Co., DE . He is buried at the Indian Mission Church with his wife, Lydia Ann Wright . Lydia was born on 2 February, 1848 and died 3 May, 1901. Her photo can be found in the Nanticoke Indian Photo Book. Robert appears with his parents in the 1850 and 1860 DE. census records. By 1870, however, Robert was married and living in his own household with his wife and 2 children (Mary Elizabeth, age 2 and John A., age 1). Living in the same household was James Wright, age 7. James was probably related to Lydia's family. Dave Wright, Lydia's uncle, and his family were living next door. Robert's occupation in 1870 was listed as "seaman". By 1880, however, he was living in Milford Hundred, Sussex Co., DE. and his occupation had changed to "farmer". Robert's death certificate lists his age at the time of his death as 73 years, 10 months & 15 days. He was called a farmer, a widower and colored. The cause of death was listed as pneumonia and he was shown living in Millsboro, Indian River Hundred, Sussex Co., DE. The death certificate lists the place of burial as Johnson's Chapel which was the name of the original Indian Mission Church and, in fact, his gravemarker (and Lydia's) is to be found there. It is now much weathered and cannot be read but I copied the inscription many years ago. The death certificate lists his mother's name as "Heslin" but the census clearly lists Elizabeth or "Lizzie".
